title: Nonlinearity Encoding for Extrapolation of Neural Networks

problem.claim: Predicting unseen data outside the training distribution is a common challenge in scientific applications of physics and chemistry.

gap.claim: Neural-network extrapolation has not been extensively studied, and no universally applicable method for general regression settings had been investigated.

contributions.claim: Introduces automated nonlinearity encoder (ANE), a data-agnostic embedding method for improving neural-network extrapolation without modifying prediction-model architectures.
Applies ANE to high-throughput screening for discovering solar-cell materials.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art extrapolation accuracies across extensive scientific applications and varied data formats.
The authors report that ANE significantly improved screening accuracy in the solar-cell-materials application.

narrative_sequence.summary: Extrapolation beyond the training distribution is a recurring challenge in physics and chemistry applications.
Neural-network extrapolation is understudied, with no generally applicable method identified for general regression.
ANE uses data-agnostic embedding to linearize input-to-target relationships without architectural changes.
The authors report strong extrapolation accuracy across scientific applications and data formats.
ANE was applied to solar-cell-material screening, where the authors report improved screening accuracy.

source_observation.claim: The method improves extrapolation by embedding data to conversely linearize the original input-to-target relationships.

interpretation.claim: Transforming the representation may address extrapolation behavior without changing the predictor architecture.

application.claim: For regression tasks requiring predictions beyond the training distribution, consider representation-level transformations before architectural changes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy works beyond the reported scientific applications and data formats.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the ANE algorithm or embedding construction.
The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, metrics, numerical results, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
